GBIF  (2)

discussion: COMMENTS The only report of this species in New Caledonia is from E. G. Paris (1906, 1910) as Chiloscyphus cymbaliferus. The two specimens in his herbarium kept at Rennes University (REN) are not different from Tetracymbaliella comptonii. Therefore, T. cymbalifera must be removed from the New Caledonian flora.

materials_examined: Type: New Zealand. Auckland Islands, not seen. SPECIMEN EXAMINED. — New Caledonia. South Province, Mt. Mou, VII. 1909, Le Rat s. n. as “ Chiloscyphus cymbaliferus ” (REN); Mt. Dzumac, “ ad arbores in silvat., 1000 m alt ”, VII. 1905, Le Rat s. n. as “ Chiloscyphus cymbaliferus ” (REN).

SOUTHERN_AUS_FIELD_GUIDE  (1) 
This Fommon species grows mainly on soil and rotting logs in wet
 forest and rainforest. The shoots are typically 5 mm wide, pale
·yellow through green to brownish-green. The leaves.are straight­
 sided, the sides drawing closer together towards the leaf apex, where
 there is a small tooth at each corner. These teeth can be much reduced
 or even absent. The underleaves are circular, with numerous teeth
 around the margin.

H. conjugatue Lophocoleaceae                                                         TV
This species is recognised by the more or less upright shoots
with hooded tips.The leaves are concave so that the shoots appear
to be almost tubular, and the leaf margins are entire, except for
occasional teeth on the dorsal margin near the leaf base (invisible
in the field). The underleaves are also concave and entire and
are not much smaller than the leaves.
    H circumdentatus (T) is similar in appearance in the field,         H. conjugatus
but the leaves and underleaves are toothed all around.
    H cymbaliferus (TV) - Tetracymbaliella cymbalifera of Scott (1985) - is
remark�ble in having semicircular sacs on leaves and lobes. It is a very small species,
and the leaves are curled around the stem so that the structure is rather hard to see.

appearance is a little like Plagiochila fasciculata. The
bean-shaped underleaves are deeply incised and carry several
long, spine-like teeth.                                                  �
